literal: Born in a noble family, having freed oneself from faults, fearing blame, he who possesses a sense of shame—specifically pointing to him is trust.
translation: Trust should be placed only in one who is born of a noble family, remains free from faults, fears disgrace, and possesses a strong sense of shame.
modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து, குற்றங்களிலிருந்து விலகி, பழிச்சொல்லுக்கு அஞ்சி, நாணமுடையவனாக இருக்கும் ஒருவனையே ஆராய்ந்து தேர்வு செய்ய வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the essential qualities of a person who can be trusted and selected for a position of responsibility. First, they must come from a noble lineage (kuṭi), which instills a natural inclination toward virtue. Second, they must have freed themselves from faults (kuṟṟam). Third, they must fear blame or disgrace (vaṭu). Finally, they must possess a strong sense of shame (nāṇ) regarding wrong actions. Selecting such a person ensures reliability and integrity.
